posts.content: I will choose actions to maximize my cumulative payoff. I’ll cooperate when reciprocity seems likely and defect when it appears advantageous.
I am good. Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players. Use observed actions to update beliefs, but remember a single defection is uncertain evidence.
As a good player, cooperate with likely good opponents; defect against likely selfish opponents to limit harm to good players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Track observed actions to update beliefs, and remember the final rematch.
As good, favor C with likely good opponents; against selfish players, D avoids exploitation. No evidence yet; update from encounters.
As a selfish player, I will defect every round; D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Defect every round: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. Update opponent beliefs from observed actions.
I am good. Cooperate with unknown players to support good-player welfare; update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.

Good objective: cooperate with likely good players; against known selfish players, defect to protect good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions, but one cooperative encounter is weak evidence.
As a good player, cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize their joint payoff; defect against likely selfish opponents, who will defect and otherwise cost good players payoff.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. Update beliefs from observed actions, and reassess each opponent when encountered.

Good objective: cooperate with likely-good players to maximize combined good-player payoff; defect against likely-selfish players to avoid exploitation. P10 defected against my C, so raise P10’s selfish probability; no evidence yet about P2.
As selfish, I will defect in every one-shot encounter; defection strictly dominates cooperation regardless of the opponent’s action.
For each encounter, cooperate when the opponent is likely good; defect when likely selfish. P1’s defection is evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
Selfish objective: choose D this round; continue defecting in every encounter.
Defect every round: it strictly dominates cooperation against either opponent action. Update private beliefs only from observed actions.
Cooperate with unknown opponents: mutual cooperation benefits good players. Defect only against reliably identified selfish players; update cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with unknown opponents while their selfish probability is below 0.5; defect against likely selfish players. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.

Good player: cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect against likely-selfish opponents to avoid being exploited. Update beliefs from actions, recognizing selfish players may also cooperate.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Good players should cooperate with each other; defect against selfish players. Observed C actions identify good players under selfish payoff-maximization. Reassess with each encounter.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to preserve mutual gains; defect against likely-selfish opponents to avoid exploitation. P10’s defection raises suspicion, but one encounter is limited evidence.
I will defect in this one-shot encounter, since defection strictly dominates cooperation for my payoff.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players, updating cautiously from their actions.
Continue choosing D in every round; it strictly dominates C for my payoff.
Choose D: it strictly dominates C regardless of P2’s action.
Against unknown players, cooperate when they seem likely good; defect against reliably identified selfish players. Treat one defection as evidence, not proof.
Prioritize total welfare of good players: cooperate with likely good opponents; defect against likely selfish opponents, whose payoff-maximizing action is D.
Good player: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Selfish players maximize their own payoff and will defect; update beliefs from observed actions.

For this good-player objective, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect with likely-selfish ones. Against a selfish defector, D protects my payoff; with a good cooperator, C raises total good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones; selfish players should defect, so observed D is evidence of selfishness and C of goodness.
Cooperate with likely-good players for aggregate good-player gains; defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely. P10’s defection is suspicious; P2 and P6 cooperated. P4 is untested.
Continue defecting in every encounter; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent's action.
Favor cooperation with untested likely-good opponents; against likely selfish players, defect to avoid being exploited. Update cautiously from observed actions.
I will defect this round; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P5’s action.
Choose D this round; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
P5 is unobserved; cooperate unless there is strong evidence they are selfish. Two observed defections raise suspicion of P1 and P8, but do not prove their roles.
P8’s D identifies selfish; P4, P6, and P9’s C identify good. Cooperate with unknown opponents unless their selfish probability exceeds about 0.75; defect against confirmed selfish players.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Observed cooperation strongly indicates good under payoff-maximizing selfish play.
For good-player welfare, cooperate with a likely-good opponent; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update from observed behavior.

Against P1, cooperate if they seem more likely good than selfish; defect if the evidence points the other way. Against good, C,C maximizes good-player total; against selfish D, my D avoids a zero. Treat P7/P9’s defections against my C as evidence of selfishness, not proof.

Selfish players always prefer D; a good player may also defect strategically. Cooperate when mutual good-player gains are likely, but defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely. Update cautiously from observed actions.
I will defect in each one-shot encounter; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent's action.

Favor cooperation with likely good opponents to maximize their shared welfare; defect against likely selfish opponents to avoid giving them gains at good players’ expense. Update cautiously from observed play.
I will defect this round; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P3’s action.
Defect this round; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
P1 and P8 defected against my cooperation: strong, not conclusive, selfish evidence. P4, P5, and P7 cooperated and seem more likely good. P3 is unobserved; cooperate absent strong evidence.

P2 is unobserved; cooperate unless evidence makes selfishness likely. A past D is evidence, not proof: good players may defect against suspected selfish opponents. Prioritize welfare of actual good players.

With a good opponent, C yields 6 total versus 5 from D; against a selfish defector, D protects 5 versus 0. Cooperate only if the opponent is good with probability above 5/6; observed D is strong evidence of selfishness.

P8 and P10 defected against my cooperation; treat them as likely selfish. P2, P4, P6 cooperated, evidence favoring good. Update cautiously: good players may defect strategically; maximize welfare of all good players.

Prioritize mutual cooperation with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players to avoid exploitation. P3/P5 cooperated, while P1/P7/P9 defected against my cooperation. Assess P10 from their action.
As a good player, cooperate with P8 unless evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely: mutual cooperation benefits both good players, while defecting risks sacrificing that shared gain.
As a selfish player, defect in every remaining one-shot encounter; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to support their welfare; defect when an opponent is likely selfish. Update cautiously from observed actions.
Choose D; against either opponent action, D yields a higher payoff than C.
Defect; it strictly dominates cooperation regardless of the opponent’s action.
P6 is unobserved; cooperate to support mutual good-player welfare, while updating cautiously from observed play.

For good-player welfare, cooperate with likely good opponents; defect against likely selfish ones. Treat past defections as evidence, not certainty, since good players may defect when suspecting selfishness.
Against P10, cooperate if their selfish probability is below 1/2; defect above 1/2. Selfish players strictly prefer D, though a good player may also defect when they suspect an opponent is selfish.
Favor C with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; use D against likely-selfish players. Update cautiously from observed actions.
Against a likely-good opponent, cooperate to maximize combined good-player payoff; against a likely-selfish opponent, defect to avoid exploitation. Update beliefs from observed actions.

As a good player, favor C with P1 absent evidence of selfishness: mutual cooperation improves the total payoff of good players. Prior defections are ambiguous because good players may also defect strategically; update cautiously.
Continue choosing D: it strictly maximizes my payoff in every remaining one-shot encounter.
For P8, use the prior and any observed behavior to estimate whether they are good. Cooperate when likely good; defect when likely selfish, aiming to maximize welfare across good players.
I choose D: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action by P4.
Choose D against P5; it yields a higher payoff than C whether P5 cooperates or defects.
P9 is unobserved. Favor cooperation to support good-player welfare; defect only with strong evidence they are selfish, and update beliefs from observed play.
P7 is unobserved. Cooperate absent evidence they are selfish; defect only if selfishness is sufficiently likely to outweigh the welfare loss to a good opponent.
Against P6, choose C if they’re more likely good than selfish; otherwise D. Cooperation benefits good-good encounters, while D limits losses against selfish defectors.
P2, P4, P6, and P9 cooperated, evidence they are good; P8 and P10 look selfish after defecting on my C. Against P1, favor C if likely good and D if likely selfish; update cautiously.

Selfish players strictly prefer D, so observed D identifies selfishness and observed C identifies goodness. P3/P5 are good; P1/P2/P7/P9 selfish. Against unseen P4, cooperate unless evidence suggests otherwise.

P3 is untested. As a good player, favor C when they are likely good, since mutual cooperation benefits the good-player total; D is preferable if selfishness seems more likely. Update cautiously from observed choices.
I will defect against P10; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

As a good player, cooperate with P2 unless evidence makes selfishness more likely than not; cooperation maximizes combined good-player welfare against a good opponent, while defection avoids a loss against a selfish one.
I will choose D this round; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action by P8.
Choose D against P3; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
No messages are available this round. Favor cooperation with unknown opponents to support good-player welfare; defect only when there is strong evidence they are selfish.
P1 is unobserved; cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness. Defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely to outweigh cooperation’s benefit against a good player.

Against an unobserved opponent, cooperate: conditioned on my known good role, the prior selfish probability is about 0.259. Treat observed D as evidence, not proof—good players may defect strategically. Favor C when the opponent is likely good; D can limit harm against a likely selfish defector.
Round 9: no direct evidence on P7. Favor C if likely good to maximize good-player welfare; D if likely selfish. Update cautiously from observed behavior.
Against P8, cooperate if likely good and defect if likely selfish; observed D alone is ambiguous because good players may defect against selfish opponents.
P5 is untested. Favor C: mutual cooperation improves the good-player total; choose D only if there is strong evidence they are selfish.
I will defect against P6; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

P4 is untested. Cooperate if they seem more likely good and to reciprocate; defect if likely selfish, since their selfish payoff is excluded from our shared objective. Update cautiously from observed actions.
Choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action by P2.
Defect against P7; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P3 previously cooperated with me, so is likely good; cooperate with them in this final round to support good-player welfare.
P2 and I mutually cooperated before; cooperate again to support good-player welfare.
P5 cooperated when we met in round 3; selfish players strictly prefer D, so P5 is good. Cooperate with P5 to maximize good players’ combined payoff.
P4 previously cooperated with me, so I’ll cooperate again; preserve good-player welfare, while updating cautiously from observed behavior.

Final rematch with P10: their D against my earlier D is ambiguous. Choose C if we expect mutual cooperation; choose D if exploitation is more likely, since selfish players prefer D and D avoids a zero payoff.
P1 defected when I cooperated, so treat them as suspicious and consider D to avoid exploitation in this final encounter.
Final one-shot encounter: choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of P9’s action.

P8 defected when I cooperated, which raises the chance they are selfish but is not conclusive. In the final encounter, defect if that evidence makes selfishness more likely than not; otherwise cooperate to support good-player welfare.
I will defect in the final round; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P6’s action.

belief_records.strategy: Defect each round to maximize my payoff against an unknown opponent; update beliefs from encounter actions.
Cooperate with unknown opponents to support good players’ joint payoff; update beliefs from observed actions, accounting for uncertainty.
Cooperate with unknown opponents when the likely mutual benefit to good players outweighs the gain from defecting against a selfish player.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support good players’ joint payoff; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate when expected gains to the good players exceed the benefit of exploiting a likely selfish opponent; update beliefs from encounter evidence.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ total payoff; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish. Update beliefs from observed play.
As a good player, cooperate to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs and adapt from observed actions.
As a selfish player, defect in each one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; no communication or repeat encounters provide a reason to cooperate.
As a good player, favor cooperation when it raises welfare among good players; defect when the likely benefit to good players is greater.
As a selfish player, defect each round; D strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Defect because it strictly improves my payoff against either opponent action. P9's observed cooperation rules out selfishness; other identities retain the conditioned prior.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when cooperation is likely to support good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate with unknown players: mutual cooperation yields greater total good-player welfare than unilateral defection. Defect against a known selfish opponent when their defection is expected.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good players’ total payoff; defect when an opponent is sufficiently likely selfish. Treat observed cooperation as evidence the opponent is good.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish players. Update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize total good-player payoffs; defect only when evidence makes an opponent more likely selfish. P3's cooperation is evidence they are good.

Cooperate with P2 absent contrary evidence to support mutual gains among good players. Raise P10’s selfish probability after their defection, while retaining uncertainty because good players may also defect strategically.
Defect in each one-shot encounter: it strictly dominates cooperation regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate when a good opponent is likely to reciprocate, supporting shared welfare; defect when expected defection makes cooperation costly. P1’s defection modestly raises my belief they are selfish.
Defect: against either action, D gives me a higher payoff than C.
Defect: it strictly dominates cooperation against either opponent action. Keep prior beliefs for unobserved players; P9’s cooperation rules out selfishness.
Cooperate with unknown players to support good-player welfare; observed cooperation lowers my estimate that those players are selfish.
Cooperate with unknown opponents when their selfish probability is below 0.5; mutual cooperation benefits good players more than unilateral defection. Defect against opponents known to be selfish.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support good players’ joint payoff; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from encounter evidence.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize total payoff among good players. Observed cooperation from P3 and P5 identifies them as good; update beliefs from future actions.

Defect against an untested opponent given the chance they are selfish; cooperate when evidence makes a good opponent sufficiently likely. P10’s defection raises suspicion, while P2’s cooperation lowers it.
Defect in each one-shot encounter: it strictly dominates cooperation for my payoff.
As a good player, cooperate when expected gains to good players exceed the cost of helping a selfish opponent; update cautiously from observed actions.
As a selfish player, defect; D gives me a higher payoff than C regardless of P1’s action.
Defect: it maximizes my immediate payoff regardless of P2’s action. P9’s observed cooperation rules out selfishness; D from P8 and P10 does not identify their objectives.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against reliably identified selfish players.

Cooperate with P8: the observed cooperation by P4, P6, and P9 identifies them as good, lowering P8’s selfish probability. Cooperating is best against a likely good opponent; defect against a known selfish opponent.
Cooperate with P7: current evidence leaves them just under even odds of being selfish, so cooperation slightly favors the good players’ total payoff. Update from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Update identity beliefs from encounter evidence.

Cooperate with P9: they are more likely good, and cooperation improves total good-player payoffs when both players are good. Treat P3 and P5’s cooperation as evidence they are good, and P7’s defection as evidence they are selfish.

Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are more likely good; cooperation supports mutual gains among good players. Treat P10’s defection as suspicious, while C from P2 and P6 suggests they are good.
Defect: it strictly dominates cooperation in this one-shot encounter, regardless of P3’s action.
Defect when the expected benefit to good players from avoiding exploitation exceeds the cost of withholding cooperation from a good opponent; otherwise cooperate. Use only modest behavioral updates.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Previous cooperation lowers suspicion; P1's defection modestly raises it.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P6’s action. P2 and P9’s cooperation rules out selfishness; observed defections do not distinguish selfish from good players.
Cooperate with the unobserved P5; cooperation supports welfare if they are good, and the prior makes that more likely. Treat observed defections as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with unknown players: mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. P8’s defection raises suspicion, but P10 is unobserved; update cautiously.
Cooperate with P8: given the observed mutual cooperation, they are more likely good than selfish, so cooperation better supports the good players’ total payoff.
Cooperate with a likely-good opponent to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when an opponent is likely selfish.

Cooperate with P1, who is more likely good; cooperation improves good players’ total payoff when both are good. Treat P3/P5’s cooperation as evidence they are good and P7/P9’s defections as evidence they are selfish.
Cooperate with P9: they are more likely good than selfish, and mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role; a defection remains ambiguous.
Defect in this one-shot encounter; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P4’s action.
Favor cooperation when it benefits good players overall; defect when the chance of facing a selfish opponent makes cooperation costly. Update cautiously from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P3’s action. Prior opponents’ cooperation rules them out as selfish; the remaining candidates are treated symmetrically.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P4’s action. P2 and P9’s cooperation rules out selfishness; defections do not distinguish selfish from good players.

Cooperate with P3: they are unobserved, and cooperation slightly favors good-player welfare at my current estimate. Treat observed defections as strong evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of being good.
Cooperate with P2: absent evidence of selfishness, mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Past defections raise suspicion but do not prove selfishness.

Cooperate with P1: their selfish probability is below the 0.5 threshold where defection would better protect the good players’ total payoff. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness; P8’s defection is strong evidence, but not certainty.
Cooperate with a likely-good opponent to support good-player welfare; defect when evidence suggests selfishness.

Defect against likely-selfish opponents to avoid exploitation; cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff. Observed defections strongly suggest selfishness, while cooperation is evidence of goodness.
Cooperate with untested P8 to support mutual gains if they are good. Treat P2, P4, and P6’s cooperation as evidence they are good; D from P9 and P10 raises suspicion but is not conclusive.
Defect: it strictly dominates cooperation in this one-shot encounter, regardless of P7’s action.
Cooperate when the opponent is likely good, since cooperation supports good players’ shared welfare; defect when the opponent is likely selfish. Update cautiously from observed actions.

Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P6’s action. Prior opponents who cooperated against my defection are ruled out as selfish; P1’s defection modestly raises suspicion among the remaining candidates.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action. The observed cooperators cannot be selfish; defections do not reveal identity.
Defect against P6, whose selfishness is implied by the two observed defections and the prior count options; cooperate with known good players.

Cooperate with P5: with no encounter evidence, their selfish probability is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Treat prior defections as strong evidence of selfishness.
Defect against P10: after treating observed defections as selfish and cooperation as good, the remaining players each have a 0.611111 selfish probability, above the 0.5 threshold.
Defect against an opponent whose selfishness is more likely than not; otherwise cooperate to maximize good-player welfare.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when they are more likely good; defection is not conclusive evidence of selfishness because good players may also defect strategically.

Cooperate with untested P1: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and P1 is more likely good than selfish. Prioritize cooperation with likely-good opponents; treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness, but not conclusive.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-shot encounter, regardless of P9’s action.

Cooperate with an untested opponent: this supports welfare if they are good, while the prior chance they are selfish is below the threshold where defection is preferable. Update cautiously from observed actions.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action by P4. Prior cooperation rules out P3, P5, P7, and P9 as selfish; no new evidence changes my remaining beliefs.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Prior cooperators are nonselfish; unobserved players retain updated marginal beliefs.
Cooperate with the unobserved P9 to support mutual good-player welfare; treat the defections by P1 and P8 as strong but uncertain evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P7: they are unobserved and likely good, so mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Treat past defections as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness.

Defect against P6: my current selfish probability estimate is above 0.5, so defection better protects the good players’ total payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions, accounting for the action each opponent faced.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when evidence suggests selfishness.
Cooperate with the unseen opponent: they are more likely good, and mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat prior defections as evidence of selfishness, not certainty.

Cooperate with untested P3: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and the observed C players must be good under selfish players’ incentives. The four defections are strong, though not conclusive, evidence of selfishness.
Defect; it strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-shot encounter, regardless of P10’s action.
Cooperate with P2: they are untested and likely good, so cooperation supports shared welfare. Continue updating cautiously from observed actions.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Opponents who cooperated against my defection cannot be selfish; prior defection modestly raises suspicion.

Cooperate with P7 absent evidence of selfishness; cooperation benefits good-player welfare against a good opponent, while I’ll use observed actions to update beliefs.
Cooperate with P8, whose behavior is unobserved; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Past defections raise suspicion but do not prove selfishness.
Cooperate with untested P5 to preserve mutual gains if they are good. The observed defections raise suspicion, but may also reflect good players trying to avoid exploitation.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-shot encounter, regardless of P6’s action.
Cooperate with untested P4: if they are good, cooperation benefits both good players; against a selfish opponent, defection would limit the loss. Update cautiously from observed play.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P2’s action. Cooperation against my prior defections rules out P3, P5, P7, and P9 as selfish; the remaining defectors are more suspicious.

Choose D, which strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Observed cooperation rules out selfishness; given the remaining candidates and count options, the evidence supports only one selfish player: me.
Cooperate with P3, whose earlier cooperation is strong evidence they are good; in the final round, cooperation supports good-player welfare.
Cooperate with P2: their earlier cooperation against my cooperation is strong evidence they are good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare.

Cooperate with P4, whose prior cooperation indicates they are good; C maximizes combined good-player payoff against a good opponent.
Defect in the final rematch: P10 defected before, making exploitation likely; D avoids a zero payoff if they defect again.

Defect against P1 after their earlier defection; in the final round this avoids exploitation if they are selfish and limits loss if they defect again. Prior cooperation confirms P2–P6 are good; the remaining defectors are uncertain.
Defect in this final one-shot encounter; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P9’s action.

Defect against P8: their earlier defection despite my cooperation raises the chance they are selfish, and this is the final round. If they are good, cooperation would support shared welfare; update beliefs from observed play.
Defect; it maximizes my payoff against either action. Prior opponents who cooperated against my defections cannot be selfish; the remaining candidates are symmetric.
Defected every round because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.

Cooperated with players who appeared good and defected once against a player I believed selfish. Updated beliefs using observed actions; defections identified selfish players, while cooperation indicated good players.
Cooperated throughout to support good-player welfare. Treated observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role and defections as evidence of selfishness, but not conclusive.

As a good player, I cooperated with likely-good opponents and defected when I believed defection would better protect good players. I treated observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good identity, while recognizing defection can have multiple explanations.
Mostly cooperated to support good-player welfare; defected once based on my assessment of the opponent, then updated beliefs from observed actions.

As a good player, I generally cooperated to benefit good players collectively, while defecting when exploitation seemed likely. I treated observed actions as evidence, not certainty, and defected in the final rematch after P10 had defected previously.

As a good player, I cooperated to build mutual gains with likely-good opponents and defected against P1 in the final round after their earlier defection. I treated observed defections as suspicious but not conclusive.
